entries.title: Orman Harrington Request
entries.public_description: My brother passed several years ago. He was a crafter. He made jewelry. This is all I have left of his. This was stolen by an influential elf. A powerful mage I suspect. I would ask the guards for assistance but they do not help when it involves mages or the connected, also they would ask for proof it is mine and I have none. This mage, his name is Alric. I would not ask you to try to take it from him directly, I know that is beyond your abilities. No, I was unable to seek this item out until recently. It has come to my attention that he has gifted the item away, to someone of far less means. Someone I think that is within your abilities. Her name Gilda. I suspect his wife would not like to know about her.

entries.title: The Theft
entries.public_description: Stumpy pretended to lose his balance tripping into a waitress and pulled her blouse down and Olga spat her drink out over a flame in suprise to the sudden sight. Meanwhile, using the distraction, Lysander tried to lift the necklace. Lysander failed and ended up ripping it off her neck attracting the attention of the guards and a priestess. Lysander ran but not before getting a firebolt to his ass.

entries.title: The Locket
entries.public_description: Looking at the locket after escaping Lysander saw a middle aged elven looking man inside

entries.title: Reward
entries.public_description: Collecting their reward the party neglected to tell Orman about their partial failure. They were supposed to do it unnoticed

entries.title: Caught
entries.public_description: The party fled town and made it to a village several days away. They awoke the next day to three people in their room: Alric, Virelle, and Sylwen. Virelle demanded they be executed but Alric thought that was too dull and uninteresting of a punishment. He instead sent them to his sisters as he put it. Before being banished to the fey wilds Stumpy was given a bottle of ale that Alric never asked to be returned.

entries.title: Arrival in the Fey Wilds
entries.public_description: You suddenly find yourselves standing inside a vast chamber, the air thick with the scent of blooming flowers and the rich earthiness of moss. The walls are not walls at all but living, breathing plants—intertwining vines and creeping ivy wrap around the stone, their leaves pulsing faintly with light. Thick flowers of every color imaginable hang from the ceiling like chandeliers, their petals opening and closing in rhythm with some unseen, gentle breeze.

entries.title: Dala's Request
entries.public_description: Intruders into my realm. How brave must you be to come here? I could simply send you back to the mundane, but what would be the fun in that? No, no. I have tasks that need to be done. I am bored and uninterested in such trivial things my playthings. You could do them though, I think five tasks wouldn’t take you too long, but then again time can get very stretchy out here. How many years has already passed I wonder

entries.title: First Task
entries.public_description: Frendamus is late in delivering Dala's slippers. The slippers were stolen and after some investigation a trail was followed to a warehouse owned by a Lark named Lydia. They find Lydia dancing uncontrolably in the corner. Finding the slippers they left her to her fate but not before helping themselves to some of her possessions.

entries.title: Reward
entries.public_description: Frendamus is greatly relieved you found the slippers and rewarded you with your choice of footware. She seems confused about any questions related to the purpose or abilities of her items. Olga notes some footwraps that she decides to keep. Crude at first glance—just heavy bands of leather and knotted cord—but each strap bears burn-scars, bite-marks, and dried blood. When bound tightly up the calves and feet, they flex and pulse with primal tension. The name Martha is burned into the inside of one of the straps.

entries.title: Strange Effects
entries.public_description: Olga's nose appears to grow a bit larger and Stumpy turns greenish. It is suspected that the fey food had this effect on them. Olga's sense of smell improves and Stumpy seems to need less food. These changes eventually go away after returning home

entries.title: Second Task
entries.public_description: Now. My feast draws near, and I grow bored of honeyed fruits and marrowless bones. I crave something wild. Bring me an emberboar. Alive. Chained, if you must, but breathing. I want its rage hot and thrashing when I slit its throat beneath the bloom moon.

entries.title: Wild Hunt Preperations
entries.public_description: The party located the Wild Hunt after a few weeks of waiting and gathering information. Deciding it would be reckless to show up without something to show they decide to hunt a bear. One is found and a trophy is made of it.

entries.title: Wild Hunt
entries.public_description: The path winds through twisted groves and bioluminescent thickets until the trees suddenly part, revealing a wide, slow-moving river gleaming beneath the wan light of a shifting Feywild moon. Mist surrounds the area, curling and dancing like living things. The scent of moss and wildflowers is thick in the air, mingled with the faint, metallic tang of old blood. Upon approaching they are given a riddle but are unable to solve it. Next it is requested the share a deed of valor which Stumpy does. Instead of challenging them to a duel, as is custom, the offering of the bear trophy sufficed.

entries.title: Robbing a drunk
entries.public_description: Lysander recognized Athach from the locket and decided to investigate him as subtly as he could. Athach was uninterested in talking to anyone wanting only to sulk. Stumpy challenged him to a drinking contest and won the mans most valuable possession: A name written on a piece of paper. Athach laughed as they took it mentioning how the name would get them killed. Lysander then robbed him finding several gems worth nearly a thousand gold, the most by far that Lysander had ever stolen. He also found a key with the name Orin engraved in it.

entries.title: Interesting Friends
entries.public_description: Lysander made friends with Harkon and secured a promise of a future meeting.

entries.title: Successfull Hunt
entries.public_description: The boar was killed and delivered to Dala

entries.title: Third Task
entries.public_description: Getting the boar in time for the feast Dala tasks the party to attend so that she may show you off to her guests. The party manages to acquire a false bottomed chalice, steal a ring from a rude noble, and fingerbang a drunk chick.

entries.title: Fourth Task
entries.public_description: The party is asked to help a hopeless Satyr find love.

entries.title: Shopping
entries.public_description: Olga manages to get an axe crafted using the axe blade stolen from Lydia. Stumpy purchases a set of armbands with the name Narn on it trading away his knowledge of a skill. Lysander buys some thieving equipment and convinces the shopkeeper to help him out. Since the shop keeper also hates Severus she gifts Lysander a ring with the name Petey scrawled on it.

entries.title: Getting a Goat Laid
entries.public_description: Trying to get Beau laid proves nearly impossible, and the party decides to give up looking. Instead Olga decides to sleep with him and hope Dala will accept that as a success

entries.title: Return to Ashwood
entries.public_description: The players find themselves back in Ashwood in the Stumbling Stag. 43 have passed

entries.title: Mayor Tamsin Holt
entries.public_description: “Gerrick Bain hasn’t come into town in three days, and now his neighbors say his farm’s gone silent. Chickens, cows—everything’s gone. I’ll give you twenty gold to take a look and come back with something useful.”

entries.title: Investigation
entries.public_description: Gerrick's house was empty, but no sign of a fight. It appeared all of his animals were led away

entries.title: Cultist
entries.public_description: Following the tracks they found two cultists complaining about wanting to kill 'that bitch'. The party quickly killed one and subdued the other only to find out they were complaining about carrying water for a cow who was the 'bitch' they were complaining about. Lysander decided they needed to kill them to avoid reprisals even though it appeared they were innocent.

entries.title: Sha’tin Cult Cave
entries.public_description: Following the tracks further they found a cave and took out the two guards, then disguised their voices and appearance (using magic) as the cultists. They tried to lure people to come out and be ambushed but the lead cultist was busy completing his ritual. He got annoyed with stumpy and used a spell to crush stumpies heart, then enthralled everyone forcing them to watch as he completed his ritual. Olga, enhanced by her legwraps, overcame the compulsion and killed him. Watching him twitching on the ground Olga felt compelled to finish him and watched as the axe drank up his essence. The other cultists were slaughtered.

entries.title: Return of the Locket
entries.public_description: Alric's locket, taken from the party before being sent to the fey wilds was found on one of the cultists. Unsure if they should take it the decision was made for them when it magically disappeared, only to be found later inside Lysander's backpack.

entries.title: Information Learned about Sha’tin
entries.public_description:
Title: The Whisper in Chains
Domain: Devils, obedience, corruption of the will.
Symbols: A broken manacle with its ends curled inward like fangs.

entries.title: Notable Loot
entries.public_description: A ceremonial dagger of blood drinking (Casts cure light wounds on self after sacrificing a creature. Effect destroys victims soul preventing reincarnation or afterlife)

entries.title: A Useful Introduction
entries.public_description:
After arriving back in town the mayor informed you that she is writing to the dutchess of Ironford to tell her of your deeds. A week later a letter arrived which disappeared before it could be read. Guessing it was an invitation by Lady Hawthorne was easy enough and the party decided to head out. When the later was later found it read as follows:

To Lysander, Olga, and Stephen,
Your recent deeds in Ashwood have not gone unnoticed. Word of your courage, resourcefulness, and success in protecting the townsfolk from grave danger has reached my attention, and I wish to extend my personal gratitude.
You are cordially invited to my estate for a feast in your honor. It is my hope to meet you in person, hear of your adventures, and discuss opportunities for further service in these lands.
Your presence will be most welcome, and arrangements will be made to ensure your comfort during your stay.
With respect and anticipation,
Lady Selara Hawthorne
Duchess of Ironford

entries.title: Bandits Mysteriously Charmed
entries.public_description: Some bandits overturned a cart feigning a need for help. They demanded a toll to pass but suddenly changed their turn once their leader fell under a charm effect. It unclear how this happened but was clear that the effect originated with Olga. There was also a few instances of items disappearing

entries.title: Rumors of Vrakka's Hand
entries.public_description: A group of angry coal burners is met and pacified with offers of alcohol and drugs. They speak about a band of raiders that sack towns carting away it's residents harassing towns. A name of a drug dealer local to Sorinks is shared

entries.title: Petey
entries.public_description: Lysander decides to try to communicate with their thief stalker by simply talking out loud hoping he will hear them. Wooden blocks with letters are created and left out with the intention of allowing their 'friend' to pick up letters to form words. It is soon learned that Lysander has a telepathic link to his ring which has been 'borrowing' his stuff.

entries.title: A Botched Bribe
entries.public_description:
Entering town Petey recognized the guard and told Lysander to bribe him. The guard insulted by this became angry and demanded to search the parties possessions. Petey continued to insist the guard's name was Ruslan even after it became clear his name was Tavik. 
Stumpy, wearing Alric's amulet, allows the female guard to look inside watching her reation carefully. She indicates her attraction to the man pictured inside mistakenly assuming he was Stumpy's lover.
The party is allowed inside

entries.title: The Offended Adventurer
entries.public_description: In town the party meets Kael and Varen. Kael gets into an argument with Stumpy which ends in  a drinking competition that Stumpy wins. Olga befriends Varen and Varen leads Kael upstairs to sleep off the drink

entries.title: The Party
entries.public_description: Lady Hawthorne throws a feast and invites adventurers and nobles including Kael and Varen. At the event, Lysander tells embellished story of their adventures - crowd loves it, Kael doesn't. A priest of Shelyn mistakenly believes Lyasander worships his goddess. Party notices Lysander now wearing a Shelyn necklace (wasn't there before). Lysander plays along

entries.title: Discrete Job
entries.public_description: Silovan Kreshholm approaches you at the party and asks you to perform a job for Lady Hawthorne. He wants the party to acquire rare herbs and return them to the mansion. 2500 gold for the job with 300 gold up front. It is made clear that this job is not to be discussed with anyone.

entries.title: Journey to Volkmar
entries.public_description: Party traveled to Volkmar over two days. Attacked by wolves en route—Lysander badly injured. Arrived and began investigating Borim's location. Petey stole a Poison of Sleeping Death. Decided to find someone who gossips. Met Tavi Redholm (halfling) and Aeris Silvaren (elf) at a tavern. Tavi was telling an exaggerated story about a wolf "two stories high" he barely escaped. Both directed party northeast—Borim likely lives in a cave. Also learned that Borim often harvests rare herbs found in the northeast

entries.title: Enslaving the Alchemist
entries.public_description: Party tracked cart tracks near herbs. Led them to Borim's cave. Borim tried to make them leave. Gary (Olga's axe) dominated Borim. Borim gave Lysander a tattoo and created the Crimson Tincture. Two lycanthropes arrived—party killed them. Gave Borim a potion of forgetfulness and made him drink it.

entries.title: Flight from Wolves
entries.public_description: The party made haste but was run down by a group of large wolves. Turning to fight they realized these were werewolves. Lysander noticed a man watching in the distance and tried to get him to help, but was unsuccessful. The wolves were killed and Olga finished off the Alpha wolf. Killing the Alpha made her axe grow in power.

entries.title: A chance Encounter
entries.public_description: Theron, exposed by Lysander, introduces himself. It is learned that he was sent to keep the party safe which he took very literally. He did not help in the fight because he believed they would live. He escorted the party back to town.

entries.title: Sacking of Sorinsk
entries.public_description:
Smoke still rises from several buildings throughout the town - thin gray columns that stain the sky. The town walls show scorch marks and broken sections. The main gate hangs crooked on its hinges.
As you approach, the devastation becomes clearer. The main street is littered with debris - broken furniture, overturned carts, shattered barrels spilling their contents. Windows are smashed. Doors hang open or have been torn from their frames.
A few townspeople move through the wreckage like ghosts, salvaging what they can. They move slowly, mechanically, in shock. Some are bandaged. Others simply stare at nothing.
    • The docks are damaged - pilings broken, debris floating in the water 
    • Several ships are missing from the harbor 
    • Guard posts are abandoned or destroyed 
    • The manor house on the hill shows signs of forced entry 
    • Many buildings are intact but looted 
    • People are alive but traumatized 
Kael and Varen fought the raiders when they hit the tavern. Varen was knocked out and dragged away.
The raiders all had Blue and Orange fish tattoos.

entries.title: Bullying a ride
entries.public_description: Theron convinces the sole remaining captain to sail you to Elredd and Highport. Kael agrees to join you. The trip will take approximately 5 days. You set sail on the Silver Surgeon with Captain Casimir Rybar. The next full moon is in four days during which time Hawthorne's brother will likely become a lycanthrope.

entries.title: Kraken
entries.public_description: The day before arriving in Elredd the ship is attacked by a Kraken. A glancing blow from the creature injures Olga but the wounds regenerate much quicker then they should. After eating about a dozen sailors the Kraken retreats into the depths.
Alric's wife. Elven woman with silver eyes. Was last seen wearing a dark crimson cloak over black leather and a silver necklace of a wasp. Worshiper of Callistria

Alric and Virelle's friend. Virelle didn't seem to like her much. Sylwen is a striking elf with angular features and long silver hair that flows like a silken veil. Her lavender eyes glow faintly in low light, and her skin carries an ethereal, almost translucent quality. She is of average elven height, graceful and slender, last seen wearing a deep violet robe adorned with silver embroidery. Her movements are fluid, and she seems to always be poised.

Alric is slender, with sharp elven features. He dresses in elegant green and gold finery, embroidered with thorn motifs and adorned with tiny bells that chime softly with his movements. Soft leather boots rise to mid-calf, supple and well-made. A silver chain rests just beneath his collar, mostly hidden. He carries a slim cane—clearly decorative, but possibly more—and a silver ring set with a black opal gleams whenever it catches the light. He never seems to give a straight answer; often speaks in rhymes or riddles. Seems constantly amused.
Middle-aged man who hired your party in Ashwood. He hired you to steal Alric's Locket

Dala Nyssira is a fey noble who agreed to send the party back home in exchange for a few tasks. She is a tall, ethereal figure with pale, green-tinged skin and piercing golden amber eyes that occasionally shimmer with light. Her long, silvery hair flows in soft waves, interwoven with flowers and ivy that slowly moves and shifts on it’s own. She wears a gown made of living flowers, each blooming with insects flying around drinking the nectar. Her movements are graceful and silent, and her voice is musical, carrying both an enchanting and commanding presence.

Eladrin Undead Skeleton Mage. A gaunt, skeletal figure clad in bark-wrapped chainmail, with a tattered cloak of autumn leaves and a massive stag skull fused to her own. Her breath fogs unnaturally warm even in the chill air.
True elf guest at the feast, distant relative of Princess Dala. Foppish, rich, arrogant, and deeply insecure
Elven noble so enraged with his former lover that he convinced the Wild Hunt to kill her.

Drug dealer in Sorinks
    • Thin, wiry build, always looks slightly underfed 
    • Pale skin, dark circles under his eyes 
    • Keeps his dark hair slicked back with too much oil 
    • Wears a faded gray coat with many pockets 
    • Nervous energy - constantly moving, twitching, fidgeting 
    • Has a habit of rubbing his fingers together
A wiry woman in her 60s with a perpetually worried expression and a sharp tongue. She's practical, skeptical of adventurers, but too desperate to turn down help.

Middle age Wood elf. Lean build, moves with absolute silence. Dark green and brown practical clothing that blends. Wears a small pin with Lady Hawthorne's crest. Lady Hawthorne's intelligence agent. Hired the party for a job
Adventurer, early 30s, barbarian
(missing) Duchess of Ironford region, lives in Sorinsk, brother is sick with lycanthropy. Kidnapped by Vrakka's Hand
(missing) Brother of Selara Hawthorne, sick with lycanthropy. Kidnapped by Vrakka's Hand
Half orc slaver, leader of Vrakka's hand
Elven noble with some magical training. Drav informed him of you and where you were hiding. He offered to help you in exchange for land and a title under Lady Hawthorne.
entries.dm_description:
Posing as a landless noble / minor wizard (divination + a few low combat spells). Came from the temple's doppelganger nest. Core trait: he reads surface thoughts — assume he knows whatever's been thought near him.

What he already knows
Petey is a sentient ring with dimensional storage and a sticky-fingers problem.
The party is walking around with a ridiculous arsenal of artifacts
He'll likely learn they carry a slip of paper bearing a true name of a devil/demon/fey — usable in Planar Binding. This is the jackpot in his eyes.

The party dangled a noble title + land for helping rescue Hawthorne. To a "landless noble," that's irresistible → he'll actually help and protect them in the near term, because the reward and the loot both require them alive and successful.

Ingratiating, useful, always says the reassuring thing (he's reading them). Volunteers "divinations" that are really laundered mind-reading — handy, and a way to steer decisions.
Works the personality-items: flatters Petey, feeds Narn a bloody tale, plays the gracious patron. Tries to become the person Petey likes (dangerous — Petey may "gift" him things).

Might try to get Silovan killed

entries.public_description: (missing) 3/4 wood elf, 1/4 orc, ranger/druid, Silovan's agent who is helping search for his employeers
(missing) Theron's lynx companion, dark gray with silver tips

Mercenary sellsword from the eastern provinces. Met at the slaver's temple where he agreed to help you escape in exchange for his life. He sheltered you in the city while you recovered from your injuries.
entries.dm_description: Doppleganger now disguised as Caelian di Soliastres

entries.public_description: (missing) Kael's companion, female rogue, understands Thieves' Cant, spoke with Lysander, open to partnership with Olga. Kidnapped by Vrakka's Hand
Helped you escape, now the captain of the Ghoul.

entries.title: The Fort (Hill Fort / "Slavers' Stockade")
entries.public_description: Approach: small stockade atop a steep hill, commanding the countryside. Surrounded by a warding ditch (20 ft wide, 10 ft deep). Only access: a road winding from the north through a narrow valley to a drawbridge.
entries.dm_description:
Walls: stone curtain wall at the drawbridge (35 ft, manned parapet). Earthen rampart + wooden stockade on W/S/E sides. Outer walls spiked downward to stop climbers. Guarded wall-walk all around.

Inside: open courtyard → 4-story gatehouse (massive, defensible all sides) → U-shaped stone keep with an enclosed garden. Dungeon level below (where prisoners/cells are). Filthy, vermin-infested, partly fire-scarred from a past sacking — repairs are crude (exploitable weak points).

Garrison leaders
Overseer / minor slave-lord — runs the fort, cruel, a fighter-mage. Suggest reskinning as Lucian de Sombra (your Koi magic-user agent, Tier 3).
Fort commander + his ogre second.
Blackthorn — ogre mage, special agent of the higher council, runs the dungeon. Reskin as a Koi enforcer.
Two humanoid clerics (goblin witch-doctor, hobgoblin shaman) — roam as wandering encounters.
Gatehouse captain + half-orc lieutenant — where caught intruders are dragged for interrogation.

Alarm & defense (defensive/delaying posture):
Gong → upper fort alerted end of that turn. Shout → next turn. Dungeon alerts one turn after the fort.
Once alerted: barracks guards take 1 turn to arm, then block ground entrances; wall guards lay down missile fire. No one found asleep/unarmed.
If the party retreats and returns: defenses strengthened, ambushes set. (They've already tipped the operation by destroying the caravan — consider the fort mildly pre-warned.)

entries.title: Journey to the Fort
entries.public_description: You traveled for 2 more days south and are now in the Drachensgrab hills. A child snuck into your camp and poisoned your stew. Cottonballs heard him, and you found the tracks to your stew. Afterwards Caelian forced the Cleric captive to drink the soup confirming it was poisoned with a sleeping agent.

entries.title: Wildmen's Quandary
entries.public_description: A small tribe of wild humans clings to life in the Drachensgrab hills, hunted by the humanoids as fair game. A humanoid tribe has captured most of their women, children, and elders, and a vile religious ceremony is approaching — the captives die unless freed soon. The wildmen assumed you were with them and tried to poison you. Lysander convinced them that you were friendly.

entries.title: Wildmen of Note
entries.dm_description:
Chieftain Morag (Tier ~1; CG hunter-chief) — desperate, proud leader. A capable tracker and warrior (surprise, bonus vs. giant-kin), but his band is too few to assault the humanoids head-on. Give him a personal stake: name one captive his own — e.g., his daughter Yorga among those taken — so the clock is personal, not abstract.

Witch Doctor Kotto (Tier ~1; NG cleric-mage) — the brains of the tribe and the architect of the capture plan. Spell kit worth knowing: invisibility, scare, ventriloquism, push, affect normal fires, light, speak with animals, chant, cure light wounds (x2). He's the one who drugs and disguises; in a fight he's support, not a bruiser.

The Captives — the majority of the tribe's non-hunters, held in the humanoid village awaiting the ceremony. The emotional core and the ticking clock. Naming two or three (a mother, a small child, the chief's daughter) makes the rescue land.

The Camp Remnant — back at the wildmen camp: two young children and one aged crone, nearly defenseless. Underlines how close to extinction the tribe is.

The Humanoid Captors — whichever tribe holds the territory the party is in: goblins, gnolls, or flinds. Their village (and chief) is the raid target. Pick the tribe by where the encounter lands and give the chief a name for the raid — a gnoll pack-lord or goblin king (Tier 1–2) presiding over the coming ceremony.

The Wildman Scout — first contact for many paths: a lone human spotted spying, who flees the instant he's seen. He's the tribe's eyes, reporting whether the party behaves like slavers or like something else.

entries.title: Kesser Reversal Table
entries.public_description:
die: 10
  entries:
    1: Disaster: "Channel Successes are added or subtracted, whichever is worse for the cleric, to all checks."
    2: Backfire: "Attack causes a magical explosion. The damage dealt is dealt again to all creatures within 30'. A Charisma check against Channel Successes can reduce the damage taken by half."
    3: Sympathy
      effect: "Both attacker, channeler, and target take the attack's damage in full. Channeler can choose to increase or decrease damage by Channel Successes but must make the same choice for all affected creatures."
    4: Counter: "The target gets a free weapon attack after this attack resolves with starting successes equal to Channel Successes."
    5: Wild Deflection: "Attack changes target to a random creature in range instead — channeler picks if ties."
    6: Reversal: "Attacker and target swap tiers and dice for the attack."
    7: Surprise: "Target is flatfooted for this attack and all dice spent on defence are lost. Channeler can choose to increase or reduce damage dealt by Channel Successes."
    8: Naked: "Attacker's sword and target's armor teleport to a random square within 30'. Both gain a Charisma save against Channel Successes to resist. If a weapon teleports, the attack still resolves with a natural attack instead."
    9: Lucky Break: "All creatures gain a luck bonus or penalty on their roll equal to Channel Successes."
    10: Crit: "Channel Successes are added or subtracted, whichever is best for the channeler, to all checks."

entries.title: Caravan Ambush
entries.public_description: Caelian di Soliastres led you to a slave caravan. The voyage took 3 days and you successfully ambushed them. The cleric leader was uncooperative, but Caelian believed he could still provide information. You agree to keep him alive but slaughtered the rest of the crew.

entries.title: The Escaped Slave
entries.public_description: As the party comes within sight of the fort, they spot a lone figure getting out — scrambling down a rope from a high window in the curtain wall's upper west stretch, dropping past the ditch, and bolting.
entries.dm_description:
”I escaped by hiding in the courtyard after the caravan arrived. I was not
counted, and so after waiting for darkness, I worked my way to the outer wall. There I found rope and clambered down from the second story. I know little of the defenses, my friends, but I do know that hobgoblins are many within the stockade, and some weird snuffling creature helps them guard the walls. It almost caught me. 1 could hear it’s snuffling noises as it came nearer and nearer. A wind came up, though, and the moan of
it screened out the snuffling noises. When the wind died down, I could hear nothing. It must have been the providence of the gods that I was not caught then.”

What he gives (let it come out in fragments):


The upper west wing is sealed and the garrison won't enter it — they think it's haunted. There's a window you can rope up to, and stairs down from it into the courtyard. (The bypass.)
A warning baked into his trauma: the stairs are rigged — a flash that blinds, then glass everywhere and people falling down the steps. (The glass-globe trap — now fair-warned.)
"Something's up there." Cold, moaning, shadows of men fighting. He won't go back. (The haunt, Jon — foreshadowed, not explained.)
Incidental fort color: the mud by the gate ("don't cross the middle"), the war dogs, that slaves get marched out in work details (seeds the disguise-exit idea).

entries.title: Drawbridge & Outer Gate
entries.public_description:
The road claws up the last of the hill and dead-ends at a deep ditch. Across it, a raised drawbridge and a lowered portcullis seal a stone gate-tower thirty-five feet high, its parapet toothed with downward spikes. Arrow slits watch the road every few paces.

Ditch: 20 ft wide, 10 ft deep, rings the whole fort.

Gate: drawbridge up, portcullis down.
entries.dm_description:
The winches are inside (area 4), triple-locked; keys on a barracks sergeant (8b west).
Bypassed entirely by the haunted-wing route (Zone 2) or talked through with the slaver bluff (if they have the gate sign).
Connects: north road ↔ drawbridge tunnel (4-area crossing); the curtain wall (Zone 2) flanks the gate above.

entries.title: ZONE 2 — The Curtain Wall
entries.dm_description:
1a — Wall-Walk (East & West)

A narrow, moonlit walk along the top of the wall, maybe five feet wide, the outer rim set with iron spikes. Loose stones are piled at intervals — ready to be hurled down.

Occupants: 2 Orc Wall Crossbowmen (368) or Hobgoblin Troopers (365) per section; one always lunges to raise the alarm.
East walkway: a heavily barred trapdoor in the floor drops to the haunted wing; guards fire at anything coming up through it at +4 to hit while shouting the alarm.
Connects: down via 1c ladder to the courtyard; to the haunted wing (2) via the barred trapdoor (which the guards refuse to use).


1b — West Guard House

A cramped bunkroom, a coal fire smoldering in the corner. A halfling's skull is nailed to the door at eye height.

Occupants: 2 Hobgoblin Troopers (365), one asleep.
Connects: 1a, 1c.


1c — Gatehouse Inner Room

Crates of salted food stacked to the ceiling, a two-piece ladder leaned against the wall.

A toppling crate is a good noise cue. The ladder is how the guards reach the wall-walk without using the haunted stair.
Connects: 1b, 1d, wall-walk.


1d — East Guard House

Bunks and a scarred table; a crow shifts on its perch and fixes you with a black eye.

Occupants: 2 Hobgoblin Troopers (365) + 1 Hobgoblin Sergeant (366) with the pet crow.
Loot: small coin, a carved wooden hawk (25 sp).
Connects: 1a, 1c.

entries.title: ZONE 3 — The Haunted Wing
entries.dm_description:
The air changes the moment you're inside — colder, still, wrong. The hobgoblins shun this whole floor; no torch is lit here. This is the stealth lane.

2a — West Walkway (rope entry)

A slops window opens onto the ditch; a knotted rope still hangs from it. Inside, dust, old bloodstains, and silence.

The party's way in (rope up from the ditch) and the escaped slave's way out.
High-Wisdom characters feel watched. Connects: 2b.


2b — West Guard Post

An abandoned post, bones scattered across the floor — the remains of men who died at their stations.

The bones are Jon's comrades' last stand (lore tie to the haunt). Connects: 2a, 2c.


2c — The Stairs (TRAP)

A flight of stone steps down toward a latched door. Faint glints catch the light near the treads.

Three trip-wires, three separate find-traps checks — miss any one and it trips. Triggered:

Foot of stairs: flash bursts — blinds everyone present for 4 rounds, no save.
Head of stairs: ~3,000 glass beads scatter; anyone on that spot takes 1d6.
Pile-up: after one round, the first character to move without declaring caution slips and tumbles down, dragging others with them — 1d6 + 1 per person who lands on them. Avoid by crawling / sweeping beads / not moving while blind.

No guards investigate (they won't enter). Loud but raises no alarm.
Top of stairs is bricked up; bottom door self-latches behind the party (inside-only latch; reopen with a dagger, 2 rounds) and opens into the outer courtyard (5).
Connects: 2b ↔ 2d ↔ down to courtyard.


2d — Room Over the Gate

Murder holes look down on the drawbridge avenue. A heavy winch sits locked in the corner beside a cask of rancid oil.

The drawbridge/portcullis winch is here but locked — the keys can work it to drop the bridge for the rest of the party.
Connects: 2c ↔ 2e.


2e — East Guard Post

A skeleton slumps against the wall, still gripping a rusted blade. The faint clash of battle seems to rise and fade in the edge of hearing.

Battle-sounds (save vs. spells to hear) — telegraph for the haunt next door. Connects: 2d ↔ 2f.


2f — The Haunt (Sergeant Jon, 382)

Light flickers without a source. A glowing mist gathers, resolving into a gaunt man with black hollows for eyes, reaching toward you.

Jon (382) — area-bound within ~60 ft, defends this stretch and the trapdoor. Run all ghost layers by hand: touch drains 2 Dex (no save); at Dex 0 he possesses; opposite-alignment bodies he strangles instead (1, 2, 4, 8…); immune to non-silver/non-magic weapons; can't be turned; only exorcism ends him.
The answer is to leave — step out of his area and the threat ends; withdrawing satisfies his duty and may lay him to rest. Hold person ejects him from a possessed body.
Hidden under a floor-stone: a small coin cache + a ruby ring (revealed by possession or a search).
Connects: 2e; barred trapdoor up to 1a (east).

entries.title: ZONE 4 — The Gate Crossing
entries.dm_description:
4 — Winch Room

A low stone chamber; two great winches stand wound and locked. Pale spiders drift across the ceiling, glowing faintly.

The spiders are harmless. Winches: 3 locks each; keys on the 8b west-tower sergeant. Working a winch lowers the bridge/portcullis.
Connects: drawbridge tunnel, outer courtyard.


5 — Outer Courtyard (ANKHEG)

An open yard between the curtain wall and the gatehouse. A broad patch of churned mud fronts the inner gate. The crickets go suddenly, completely silent.

Buried ankheg (381) in the 30-ft mud morass — the silence is the tell (high-TN awareness to avoid surprise). Run by hand: hard carapace vs. easy belly (1–2 attackers/round), bite hurls prone into the mud, acid line at ~half HP.
Its death-wail raises the fort alarm regardless of how quiet the fight was. The mud cuts movement to ¼; a faller loses a round.
Portcullis jammed ~1 ft up: crawl under to reach the entryway.
Connects: winch room / haunted-wing stair (in), entryway (out).


Entryway of Fire (TRAP — if alarmed)

A narrow gate-tunnel, twenty feet of stone with dark murder holes overhead.

Armed only if the alarm is already up. Flaming oil pours from the holes, igniting stacked goods. Within 10 ft of the blaze: 1d4/round; running the channel ~3 damage per segment (save halves; wet blanket / courtyard mud drops it to 1/segment, no save). Wall guards add arrow fire (poor angle at the entry, deadly if the party flees back across the courtyard).
If the ankheg was beaten silently and no alarm went up, this never arms.
Connects: courtyard ↔ gatehouse / parade ground.



ZONE 5 — The Gatehouse (7–8) · the garrison hub

Avoid, don't clear. The gatehouse is built to pin intruders in one room and bury them in bodies. Roving patrol: 4 Hobgoblin Troopers (365) + 1 Sergeant (366), 1-in-6 per turn.

7a — Stables

Oxen and horses shift in their stalls; three heavy wagons stand ready. A hayloft looms ten feet up. A large iron gong hangs by the door.


Occupants: 2 young Hobgoblin Troopers (365).
The gong: ringing it brings 6–30 hobgoblins boiling out in 1 turn. The single worst noise in the fort — kill the two quietly or the assault is over before it starts.
Connects: parade ground, 8b.


7b / 8a — Stair Rooms & Spy-Hole Door

A padlocked, iron-barred door with a sliding spy-hole. A gruff voice demands the word.

Password-gated — and the party has none unless they pried the gate sign from the caravan cleric. Occupants: 2 Hobgoblin Troopers (365) + 2 Goblin Skulkers (379) with halberds.
Connects: up into 8b.


8b — Gatehouse Barracks

Tier on tier of bunks and weapon racks across three connected towers, thick with the smell of unwashed bodies.

Occupants (the bulk of the garrison): ~22 Hobgoblin Troopers (365) + 2 Sergeants (366) in the main hall; ~10 + a sergeant in the east tower; 4 over the gate tending the hot-oil pots (murder-hole trap — poured on anyone below the gate if the alarm sounds); ~10 + a sergeant in the west tower with a rack of 17 light crossbows and the winch keys on the sergeant's belt.
This is the room a frontal assault dies in. Connects: 7a, 8a, 8c, 8d.


8c — Captain of the Gatehouse (interrogation room)

A banded-mail officer rises from a table strewn with manifests; a second looms behind him. A cluster of iron keys hangs on a peg, and a trapdoor sits in the ceiling.

Occupants: Captain Gorbin (361) — hidden loaded crossbow, sword "Sundancer" — and Lieutenant Kairn (362), greatsword "Winnower." Caught intruders are dragged here.
Keys to all gatehouse + curtain-wall doors on the wall peg. Ceiling trapdoor calls barracks troops down.
Connects: 8b, up to 8d / the keep.


8d — Inner Wall-Walk

A walkway overlooking the open muster yard below.

Occupants: Hobgoblin Troopers (368/365) on watch — they can see the whole parade ground, so crossing it openly is spotted from here.
Connects: 8b/8c ↔ parade ground.

Occupants: 2 young Hobgoblin Troopers (365).
The gong: ringing it brings 6–30 hobgoblins boiling out in 1 turn. The single worst noise in the fort — kill the two quietly or the assault is over before it starts.
Connects: parade ground, 8b.


7b / 8a — Stair Rooms & Spy-Hole Door

Password-gated — and the party has none unless they pried the gate sign from the caravan cleric. Occupants: 2 Hobgoblin Troopers (365) + 2 Goblin Skulkers (379) with halberds.

8b — Gatehouse Barracks

Tier on tier of bunks and weapon racks across three connected towers, thick with the smell of unwashed bodies.

Occupants (the bulk of the garrison): ~22 Hobgoblin Troopers (365) + 2 Sergeants (366) in the main hall; ~10 + a sergeant in the east tower; 4 over the gate tending the hot-oil pots (murder-hole trap — poured on anyone below the gate if the alarm sounds); ~10 + a sergeant in the west tower with a rack of 17 light crossbows and the winch keys on the sergeant's belt.

8c — Captain of the Gatehouse (interrogation room)

A banded-mail officer rises from a table strewn with manifests; a second looms behind him. A cluster of iron keys hangs on a peg, and a trapdoor sits in the ceiling.

Occupants: Captain Gorbin (361) — hidden loaded crossbow, sword "Sundancer" — and Lieutenant Kairn (362), greatsword "Winnower." Caught intruders are dragged here.
Keys to all gatehouse + curtain-wall doors on the wall peg. Ceiling trapdoor calls barracks troops down.

8d — Inner Wall-Walk

A walkway overlooking the open muster yard below.

Connects: 8b/8c ↔ parade ground.

entries.title: ZONE 6 — The Inner Keep (condensed/adapted)
entries.dm_description:
Parade Ground

A wide muster yard of packed earth, roughly eighty feet by sixty. Something large and four-legged lifts its head and growls; further off, a hunched shape lopes along the far wall.

Occupants: 2–4 Fort War Dogs (370) loose (attack any non-resident scent) and 1–2 Carnivorous Apes (369) roaming "for food." Watched from 8d above.
The hub: every keep door and the dungeon stair open off it.
Connects: gatehouse (N); Overseer's Hall, Commander's Quarters, Executioner's Post, Shaman's Shrine, Slave Pens, Dungeon Stair.


Overseer's Hall

A cold stone hall hung with a few looted tapestries; an iron-bound strongbox sits behind a heavy chair. A robed figure turns, and a goblin at her side bares its teeth as a white-furred wolf rises.

Occupants: Hill Fort Overseer (357) [Tier 3 boss], Witch-Doctor Guliyet (363), and her Winter Wolf (380) (Guliyet's whistle also summons it if she's met elsewhere).
Strongbox: her key (equipment file). A private passage runs from here down to the dungeon stair — a back way to Silovan that skips the parade ground.
Connects: parade ground; private passage → dungeon stair.


Commander's Quarters

A spartan room, everything bolted in place — table, chair, chest — as if arranged for someone who cannot see. A narrow closet door is chained shut, and from behind it comes a faint dry slithering.

Occupants: Fort Commander Icar (358) [Tier 2, blind — fights by memory and sound, treat as blindsight in the fort]. In the chained closet: the Captive Medusa (371), guarding his cache; Icar's Periapt of Proof Against Poison is why he's unharmed near her.
Freeing the medusa turns her loose on the garrison — a major lever. Icar's cache (coin, gems, potions) is in the closet she guards.
Connects: parade ground.


Executioner's Post

A blood-darkened block stands in a fenced yard beside the pens; a hulking ogre leans on a notched axe.

Occupant: The Executioner (359) [ogre]. Carries out the Overseer's sentences; positioned between the parade ground and the slave pens.
Connects: parade ground, slave pens.


Shaman's Shrine

A reeking shrine of bone and hide, daubed with old blood; a hobgoblin in fetishes looks up mid-chant.

Occupants: Shaman Adhu Nazaryet (364) + 2–8 Hobgoblin Troopers (365) at worship.
Connects: parade ground.


Slave Pens (rescue: Doran, Varen-rogue)

Barred cells along a filthy run, packed with chained, branded captives. Goblins with keys lounge by the gate, bored.

Captives: Doran Svetov and Varen-the-rogue, plus generic townsfolk/wildman captives. Turnkeys: 2–4 Goblin Skulkers (379).
The revolt lever: these prisoners will fight their captors given a chance and weapons. Freeing and arming them is the party's best distraction force. (Coffle them back up for the disguised exit.)
Connects: parade ground, Executioner's post, dungeon stair.

entries.title: ZONE 7 — The Dungeon (condensed/adapted) · wakes 1 turn after the fort
entries.dm_description:
Dungeon Stair

A guarded stair (or a trapdoor beneath the Overseer's hall) drops into damp dark.

Reaching the dungeon before the alarm is the goal — once the upper fort wakes, this level follows one turn later.
Connects: parade ground / Overseer's private passage → Warden's Hall.


Warden's Hall

A vaulted undercroft lit by greasy torches. A massive horned figure unfolds from a chair, far too calm to be afraid.

Occupant: Dungeon Warden (360) [Tier 3 oni / Koi agent]. Run his ogre-mage tricks by hand (invisibility, flight, charm, gaseous form, regeneration, a once-daily cone of cold). He knows the onward route to the stronghold and carries the Sigil of the Koi Council (proof of who runs the fort) and the master cell ring.
Connects: dungeon stair, cells, the pit.


Interrogation Cells (SILOVAN — primary objective)

A short cell block, one door reinforced. Inside, a battered wood-elf looks up — alive, watchful, worked-over.

Captive: Silovan — held for interrogation, not sale. Clock: he may break or be near death; freeing him also gets the party someone who can later unmask Callihan. Turnkeys: 1–2 Goblin Skulkers (379).
Connects: Warden's Hall.


The Pit / Feeding Den

A reeking shaft in the floor; below, things move and gibber, and old bones crunch underfoot.

Where prisoners the Overseer is "done with" are fed to the Carnivorous Apes (369) (1–3). A grim hazard and a place a body can vanish.
Connects: cell block.
